thread:
kevin: RFC follow-up: need a crisp ownership model for canary fallbacks. Router/runtime/controller: who is the last-resort authority, and how do we make behavior auditable and deterministic?

leah: +1. Proposal: split responsibility into three "buckets":
- policy (controller): declares targets, thresholds, rehab windows
- fast-path (runtime): per-request fast-fail/hedge w/ conservative thresholds
- coordination (router): lease checks, sampling to controller, and durable audit events
Keep controller as truth, but accept local decisions when lease missing.

omar: Important: deterministic tie-breaker for split decisions. If multiple local nodes decide, we must avoid flip-flopping. Suggest consistent-hash on request-id + variant-seed so rollouts are reproducible. Example pseudocode: 

```
# deterministic routing tie-breaker
seed = controller_policy.seed
variant = hash(request_id || seed) % 100 < policy_pct ? new_variant : control
```

leah: Agree. Also require a lease TTL from controller for rollouts (e.g., 30s). Router checks lease before forwarding control decisions. If lease expired, router consults runtime heuristics + deterministic tie-breaker.

tess: Telemetry + audit: every local fallback must emit an audit event with: decision_ts, request_id (sampled), node_id, reason (metric + threshold), fallback_variant, policy_version. Events go to rollout.signals and audit.events topic. Keep payload small (avoid full traces).

kevin: API surface thoughts: router exposes lightweight endpoints for controller to push policies (PATCH /v1/rollouts/:id) and runtime exposes a local query (GET /local/fallback-decision?req=...) for debug. For machine-to-machine, use a versioned protobuf: fields = [policy_id, seed, percentage, lease_expires_at].

omar: Error semantics: prefer explicit codes so callers can interpret and react: 200 (decision), 202 (deferred-to-controller), 409 (policy-mismatch), 503 (no-capacity/local-shed). Router should translate internal heuristics to these codes.

leah: Cost tradeoffs: heavy sampling to controller is expensive. Suggest sample windows: 1% of requests when stable, 10% during suspect windows. Router should backoff sampling if controller lag > 200ms.

tess: Cardinality limits on signals: emit aggregate metrics per minute + sampled raw events. Metric names small: roll.p99, roll.err_rate_5m, roll.rehab_count. Keep label set: model_id, region, policy_id.

ops-bot: rollout-controller: policy v1.2 applied to cluster eu-central-1 at 2026-03-22T09:40:00Z

kevin: Operational runbook bits: if controller partition detected (lease loss), routers flip to deterministic mode and emit a 'local-fallback-mode' event. Manual override endpoint (/v1/rollouts/:id/force-off) for SRE.

omar: Also add a bounded retry/hedge in runtime: single extra attempt to fallback variant, no more than 50ms extra latency budget. Hedge attempts must be counted in audit.

leah: For RFC: I'll draft the ownership diagram + sequence diagrams (policy push, steady-state routing, partition handling). Tess will write the audit schema and sampling knobs.

tess: Will do. I'll include example protobuf and a JSON debug payload for ops.

kevin: Thanks team. Action items: (1) leah: sequence diagrams + deterministic tie-breaker rules (2) tess: audit schema + metric list + sampling policy (3) omar: small runtime hedging perf notes + latency budget. I'll assemble into RFC and tag arch for review. /cc @tess @omar @leah
